ig_carousel_topic.topic: Bankroll math for people who've never thought about bankroll
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
How much of your bankroll should you bet on a single game?
Most people guess. The math has a real answer.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common mistake: flat-betting whatever feels right.
Some nights that's 5%. Some nights 25%. Both from the same account.
That inconsistency kills long-term results even when picks are winning.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
The standard approach is flat-unit betting. Pick a unit size, 1-2% of your total bankroll, and bet that amount on every play.
At 54% win rate, consistency compounds. Variance doesn't wipe you out.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example: $1,000 bankroll. One unit = $10 (1%).
A 3-2 day at standard odds nets roughly +$8-$12.
A brutal 1-4 day costs about $30. You're still in business tomorrow.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
The goal isn't to maximize one winning week.
It's to still be betting in month six.
Unit discipline is what separates a 54% bettor who profits from one who breaks even.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Bankroll sizing isn't glamorous but it's where most people leak money. One unit, every game, same size. The math works if you let it.
